[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/slowcooker)](https://pypi.org/project/slowcooker/)

1.5D core transport for tokamaks and stellarators. [TORAX](https://github.com/google-deepmind/torax)
(unchanged, pinned) solves the transport equations; slowcooker gives it

- the **geometry of any equilibrium**: flux-surface averages from [GVEC](https://gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/gvec-group/gvec)
  for tokamaks and stellarators, passed in through TORAX's CHEASE format, in memory;
- **neutral beams** from [freeofcharge](https://github.com/max-models/freeofcharge): heating, fuelling
  and current recomputed from the plasma between segments of the run;
- the **equilibrium re-solved** with TORAX's pressure (the half dimension of 1.5D);
- a **stellarator neoclassical** transport model (1/ν and √ν regimes, ambipolar $E_r$) as a TORAX
  plug-in; its prefactors are still to be verified against the literature and DKES/MONKES;
- the profiles back as one xarray dataset over `t` and `rho`, ready for
  [plasma-plots](https://github.com/max-models/plasma-plots), and parameter scans.

Documentation: <https://max-models.github.io/slowcooker/>

## Install

slowcooker needs Python 3.12 or newer (TORAX's requirement). GVEC is built from source, which needs
a Fortran compiler and netCDF-Fortran (on Debian/Ubuntu:
`apt install gfortran cmake pkg-config liblapack-dev libnetcdff-dev`).

```bash
make install                 # uv sync --extra dev, plus the pre-commit hooks
pip install -e ".[gvec]"     # or with pip
```

## Example

Heat transport in W7-X with constant diffusivities, on the GVEC equilibrium that comes with slowcooker:

```python
import numpy as np

from slowcooker import base_config, gvec_geometry, profiles, run
from slowcooker.data import gvec_equilibrium

geometry = gvec_geometry(gvec_equilibrium("w7x"), rho=np.linspace(0.02, 1.0, 40))
config = base_config(geometry, density=3e19, heating=2e6, chi=0.5, t_final=1.0)
data = profiles(run(config))       # xarray over t and rho
print(data.T_e.isel(t=-1).values)
```

`base_config` writes a TORAX config dictionary; change any part of it with `slowcooker.merge`.
Couple freeofcharge's beams or a GVEC re-solve with `slowcooker.run_coupled` and
`slowcooker.nbi.NBICoupling` or `slowcooker.equilibrium.EquilibriumCoupling`; see the examples in
the documentation.

The command `slowcooker case.py -o profiles.nc` runs the `CONFIG` dictionary of a Python file and
writes the profiles.

## Development

```bash
make lint     # ruff check, ruff format --check, ssort, pyright
make test     # pytest with coverage
make docs-dev # the documentation site, live
```

Profiling regions are tagged `slowcooker` (opt-in, see
[scope-profiler](https://github.com/max-models/scope-profiler)).
